content.title: IF YOU ATE {{THIS}} EVERY DAY... YOUR BODY WOULD CHANGE FASTER THAN YOU THINK
facts: If you ate **beetroot leaves** (the whole beet, greens included) every day for 2 weeks, your leg cramps would ease and your workout endurance would climb — the nitrates and iron team up to move oxygen more efficiently.
If you ate **kimchi** every day for 3 weeks, your bloating would fade and your bathroom habits would become more regular as its live bacteria recolonize your gut.
If you ate **liver** (just 1 small serving/week) for 30 days, your energy would stop crashing by 3pm — it's one of the densest natural sources of B12 and iron on the planet.
If you ate **brazil nuts** (2 per day) for 1 week, your thyroid would get a selenium boost that helps regulate your metabolism and mood.
If you ate **kefir** every day for 2 weeks, your skin would look calmer and less inflamed as your gut bacteria diversity improves.
If you ate **mackerel** (2x/week) for 30 days, your joints would feel less stiff in the morning thanks to its heavy omega-3 load.
If you ate **chia seeds** (1 tbsp/day) for 10 days, your afternoon energy slumps would smooth out as they slow down sugar absorption.
If you ate **sauerkraut** every day for 3 weeks, your digestion would speed up and food would stop sitting heavy in your stomach.

caption:
A few of today's picks deserve a deeper look. Beetroot greens are often thrown away, but they're packed with iron and nitrates — the nitrates convert into nitric oxide in your blood, which relaxes vessels and lets oxygen reach your muscles faster, which is exactly why cramping eases. Kimchi works differently: it's fermented, so it's loaded with live bacteria strains that physically repopulate your gut lining, crowding out the bacteria that cause bloating and gas. And kefir isn't just "yogurt's cousin" — its bacterial diversity is actually higher than most yogurts, which is why it tends to calm skin inflammation faster. Everyone's gut and body chemistry is different, so give it a few weeks and listen to how yours responds.
